intro: Tourism and lake recreation drive most of the local economy here, and it's easy for landowners to think of their property purely in those terms without realizing there's an oil and gas history layered underneath. If you own minerals near Greers Ferry, that history is real, even if the county's overall shale results were more modest than the play's core.

sections.heading: Lake town, Fayetteville Shale fringe
paragraphs: The Corps of Engineers project that created Greers Ferry Lake reshaped a lot of land use in this part of Cleburne County, but the mineral estate under privately held land nearby is still subject to the same Fayetteville Shale leasing and drilling history as the rest of the county's fringe area.

sections.heading: What we check before quoting a value
paragraphs: We look at operator and permit records for your specific legal description, confirm whether a well has ever been drilled nearby, and check current production if one exists. Given how variable results are on the county's fringe, we don't rely on general assumptions about the area.
If your interest is undeveloped, we price it as such, tied to potential future activity rather than current royalty income.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership near lake-area development
paragraphs: Land near Greers Ferry Lake has changed hands more than most rural Cleburne County acreage, sometimes without minerals transferring cleanly. We check whether your specific chain of title includes the mineral estate as part of any offer.

faqs.question: Does the lake and dam project affect who owns the minerals nearby?
faqs.answer: Not directly for privately held land outside the project boundary, but land near the lake has changed hands frequently, so we verify the mineral chain of title carefully.

faqs.question: Is this part of Cleburne County part of the productive Fayetteville Shale core?
faqs.answer: No, it's on the fringe, with lower well density and more variable results than counties like Van Buren or Faulkner.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my lake-area property still includes mineral rights?
faqs.answer: We review the deed history for your specific parcel to check whether minerals were reserved or conveyed separately from the surface.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests near the lake even if there's never been a well drilled?
faqs.answer: Yes, undeveloped acreage near Greers Ferry still has potential value, and we evaluate it based on nearby activity rather than requiring existing production.
